items.article1Title: Foster + Partners' projects feature in new Living Tech Gallery at Hong Kong Science Museum
items.article1Summary: Foster + Partners is part of a new permanent exhibition at the Hong Kong Science Museum, which opened to the public on 6 February. The 'Living Tech Gallery' is one of three new permanent exhibition spaces showcasing the role of design and technology in daily life.
items.article1Body:
Foster + Partners is part of a new permanent exhibition at the Hong Kong Science Museum, which opened to the public on 6 February. The 'Living Tech Gallery' is one of three new permanent exhibition spaces that explore the role of design and technology in daily life.

The exhibition features models, drawings and interactive displays from a selection of the practice's projects, including the Hong Kong International Airport, the Millau Viaduct and Apple Park. The gallery aims to inspire visitors, especially young people, to consider how architecture and engineering shape the built environment.

The Living Tech Gallery is open daily and forms part of the museum's ongoing renewal programme.
items.article2Title: Bloomberg HQ sets new benchmark for sustainable commercial architecture
items.article2Summary: The Bloomberg European Headquarters in London has been recognised for its integrated approach to sustainability, including rainwater harvesting, natural ventilation and high recycled content in materials.
items.article2Body:
The Bloomberg European Headquarters in the City of London continues to receive acclaim for its environmental performance. The building was designed with sustainability at its core, incorporating rainwater harvesting, natural ventilation strategies and a high proportion of recycled and low-impact materials.

Energy consumption is significantly lower than typical office buildings of comparable size, and the project has influenced industry standards for commercial development. The design reconnects Watling Street with the surrounding urban fabric and provides generous public spaces.
items.article3Title: Apple Park marks ten years since opening
items.article3Summary: Apple Park in Cupertino celebrates a decade as one of the world's most distinctive corporate campuses, with its ring-shaped building, extensive landscaping and focus on collaboration and wellbeing.
items.article3Body:
Apple Park in Cupertino opened in 2017 and has since become one of the most recognisable corporate campuses in the world. The 175-acre site is centred on a ring-shaped main building that accommodates over 12,000 employees.

The design prioritises landscape, natural ventilation and renewable energy. The campus includes orchards, meadows and a central courtyard, creating a working environment that blurs the boundary between building and nature. Over the past ten years, the project has been studied as a model for large-scale workplace design and sustainability.
items.article4Title: Millau Viaduct anniversary: two decades of engineering excellence
items.article4Summary: The Millau Viaduct in southern France marks its anniversary as one of the most celebrated infrastructure projects of the twenty-first century, spanning the Tarn Valley with an elegant cable-stayed structure.
items.article4Body:
The Millau Viaduct spans the Tarn Valley in southern France and was, at the time of completion, the tallest bridge in the world. Its elegant structure responds to the dramatic landscape while improving connectivity between Paris and the Mediterranean.

The viaduct has become an icon of French engineering and a reference point for long-span bridge design. Maintenance and monitoring programmes have ensured its continued performance and safety over two decades of operation.
items.article5Title: Architecture workshop for children returns to London studio
items.article5Summary: A free one-day workshop for children aged 8–12 will introduce participants to the basics of drawing, model-making and sustainable design at the Foster + Partners London studio.
items.article5Body:
The annual architecture workshop for children returns this spring, giving participants aged 8–12 the chance to work alongside designers and learn about drawing, model-making and sustainable design. The one-day event is free and takes place at the practice's London studio.

Places are limited and booking is required. The workshop is part of the practice's commitment to education and outreach, encouraging the next generation to engage with architecture and the built environment.
items.article6Title: Masdar City phase two advances with new residential and commercial plots
items.article6Summary: The next phase of Masdar City in Abu Dhabi will add residential, commercial and research facilities, continuing the development's focus on low-carbon transport and renewable energy.
items.article6Body:
Masdar City is a planned sustainable district in Abu Dhabi designed to be one of the world's most sustainable urban communities. Phase two of the development will add significant new residential, commercial and research capacity while maintaining the masterplan's emphasis on pedestrian priority, renewable energy and low-carbon transport.

The masterplan combines traditional Arabic urban patterns with advanced environmental systems, creating a model for future cities in hot climates.
items.article7Title: RIBA Award winners include Foster + Partners projects
items.article7Summary: Three Foster + Partners projects have been recognised in this year's RIBA Awards, spanning infrastructure, culture and workplace categories.
items.article7Body:
The Royal Institute of British Architects has announced the winners of this year's RIBA Awards. Three projects by Foster + Partners were among those recognised: an infrastructure scheme, a cultural building and a workplace development. The awards highlight design quality, sustainability and contribution to the public realm.

The practice congratulates the project teams and clients involved in these schemes.
items.article8Title: New digital fabrication lab opens at London studio
items.article8Summary: A new in-house digital fabrication lab will support rapid prototyping and testing of building components, strengthening the link between design, research and construction.
items.article8Body:
The practice has opened a new digital fabrication lab at its London studio. The facility supports rapid prototyping and testing of building components, from facades to structural details, and strengthens the link between design, research and construction.

The lab is equipped with 3D printers, CNC equipment and assembly spaces, enabling designers and engineers to iterate quickly and validate ideas before they are applied to full-scale projects. It will also support collaboration with universities and industry partners.
items.article9Title: Reichstag dome restoration project documented in new publication
items.article9Summary: The restoration of the Reichstag and addition of its glass dome in Berlin is the subject of a new publication that traces the design process and the building's role in German democracy.
items.article9Body:
The restoration of the Reichstag and the addition of a new glass dome in Berlin symbolise transparency and democracy. The dome allows public access and brings natural light into the parliament chamber below, while the building's energy strategy incorporates renewable sources and thermal storage.

A new publication documents the design process, the technical challenges and the building's ongoing role in German political life. The Reichstag remains one of the most visited landmarks in Berlin.
items.article10Title: Comcast Technology Center completes first decade in Philadelphia
items.article10Summary: The Comcast Technology Center, the tallest building in Philadelphia, marks ten years with a programme that includes offices, a hotel and public spaces with a vertical garden and sky lobby.
items.article10Body:
The Comcast Technology Center is the tallest building in Philadelphia and houses offices, a hotel and public spaces. A vertical garden and sky lobby activate the tower and contribute to the city skyline. The building has become a landmark for technology and innovation in the city.

Over the past decade, the centre has supported thousands of jobs and welcomed millions of visitors to its public areas and amenities.
items.article11Title: Lusail Stadium and legacy programme continue to shape Qatar
items.article11Summary: Lusail Stadium, the main venue for the FIFA World Cup 2022, is now part of a broader legacy programme that includes community facilities and ongoing events.
items.article11Body:
Lusail Stadium was the main venue for the FIFA World Cup 2022. The design draws on regional craft and light patterns, and the stadium is part of the broader development of Lusail City. Since the tournament, the venue has hosted further sporting and cultural events.

A legacy programme ensures that the stadium and surrounding infrastructure continue to serve the community and promote sport and wellbeing in Qatar.
items.article12Title: Battersea Power Station redevelopment fully open to the public
items.article12Summary: The redevelopment of Battersea Power Station on the south bank of the Thames is now complete, mixing residential, office and retail with the restored landmark.
items.article12Body:
The redevelopment of Battersea Power Station on the south bank of the Thames mixes residential, office and retail. The restored landmark and new buildings create a riverside quarter with strong connections to central London. The power station itself has been carefully restored and adapted for new uses.

The project has transformed a long-derelict site into a thriving mixed-use district, with the iconic chimneys once again defining the London skyline.
items.article13Title: Hong Kong International Airport expansion progresses
items.article13Summary: The expansion of Hong Kong International Airport continues with new concourses and improved connectivity, building on the original terminal's reputation for clarity and wayfinding.
items.article13Body:
Hong Kong International Airport at Chek Lap Kok was built on reclaimed land. The terminal's clear structure and natural lighting set a standard for airport design and wayfinding in Asia. The current expansion adds new concourses and improves connectivity for passengers and cargo.

The airport remains a critical hub for the region and a reference for future airport development.
items.article14Title: Sainsbury Centre for Visual Arts marks anniversary with new display
items.article14Summary: The Sainsbury Centre at the University of East Anglia celebrates its anniversary with a new display that reinterprets the collection within Norman Foster's single-span, naturally lit space.
items.article14Body:
The Sainsbury Centre at the University of East Anglia houses the Sainsbury collection of world art. The single-span, naturally lit space blurs the boundary between building and landscape. To mark its anniversary, the centre has opened a new display that reinterprets the collection and highlights the building's role in the campus and the region.

The centre continues to host exhibitions, research and education programmes.
items.article15Title: New research report on net-zero commercial buildings published
items.article15Summary: A new report from the practice's research group outlines design strategies for net-zero commercial buildings, drawing on lessons from recent projects.
items.article15Body:
The practice's research group has published a new report on design strategies for net-zero commercial buildings. The report draws on lessons from recent projects and sets out principles for reducing embodied and operational carbon while maintaining design quality and occupant comfort.

Key themes include passive design, renewable energy integration, material selection and the role of flexibility and adaptability in extending building life. The report is available to clients and industry partners.
items.article16Summary: Winners of the annual school design competition have been announced, with projects from secondary schools across the UK addressing sustainability and community use.
items.article16Body:
The annual school design competition encourages young people to think about the places they learn in. This year's winners have proposed schemes that address sustainability, community use and wellbeing. The competition is run in partnership with education charities and supports the national curriculum.

Winning teams will receive support to develop their ideas and present them at a national event.
items.article17Title: Space House in London to undergo careful restoration
items.article17Summary: Space House, an early example of high-density urban housing on the South Bank, is to be restored and upgraded to meet current standards while preserving its character.
items.article17Body:
Space House in London is an early example of high-density urban housing with a clear structural and servicing strategy. The building contributes to the character of the South Bank area. A programme of careful restoration and upgrade will improve energy performance and accessibility while preserving the building's character and significance.

The project will be carried out in phases to minimise disruption to residents.
items.article18Title: Willis Faber and Dumas building awarded listed status upgrade
items.article18Summary: The Willis Faber and Dumas headquarters in Ipswich has had its listed status upgraded in recognition of its importance to the high-tech movement and post-war architecture.
items.article18Body:
The Willis Faber and Dumas building in Ipswich is a landmark of high-tech architecture. The curved glass curtain wall and open-plan floors create a flexible, daylit workplace. The building has had its listed status upgraded in recognition of its importance to the high-tech movement and post-war British architecture.

The practice is working with the current owners to ensure the building is maintained and adapted sensitively for future use.
items.article19Title: Beijing Capital International Airport Terminal 3 expansion study
items.article19Summary: A study has been published on the expansion and adaptation of Terminal 3 at Beijing Capital International Airport, one of the world's largest airport buildings.
items.article19Body:
Terminal 3 at Beijing Capital International Airport was one of the world's largest airport buildings at the time of opening. The dragon-like form and colour palette reference Chinese culture and create a clear identity. A new study examines the expansion and adaptation of the terminal to meet growing demand and new operational requirements.

The study considers wayfinding, sustainability and the passenger experience in a building of exceptional scale.
items.article20Title: Zayed National Museum opens on Saadiyat Island
items.article20Summary: The Zayed National Museum on Saadiyat Island has opened to the public, celebrating the history and values of the UAE with a design that incorporates natural ventilation and tower forms evoking falcon wings.
items.article20Body:
The Zayed National Museum on Saadiyat Island celebrates the history and values of the UAE. The design incorporates natural ventilation and light, with tower forms that evoke falcon wings. The museum has opened to the public with a permanent display and programme of temporary exhibitions.

The building is part of the Saadiyat Cultural District and sits alongside other major museums and cultural institutions.
items.article21Summary: A study of the Riverside South masterplan in London's Docklands has been published, examining the mixed-use scheme's impact on the Thames and surrounding area.
items.article21Body:
Riverside South extended the development of London's Docklands with a mixed-use masterplan. The scheme proposed new connections and a balance of uses along the Thames. A new study examines the masterplan's implementation, its impact on the river and surrounding area, and lessons for future large-scale urban development.

The study is available to planning authorities and developers.
items.article22Title: Tower 2 of the World Trade Center receives design excellence award
items.article22Summary: 200 Greenwich Street (Tower 2) has received a design excellence award for its contribution to the World Trade Center redevelopment and the Manhattan skyline.
items.article22Body:
200 Greenwich Street (Tower 2) is part of the World Trade Center redevelopment. The tower's tapered form and structural system respond to the site and the memory of the original complex. The building has received a design excellence award for its contribution to the redevelopment and the Manhattan skyline.

The tower provides office space and forms part of the memorial and masterplan that has reshaped Lower Manhattan.
items.article23Title: Songdo International Business District: ten-year review
items.article23Summary: A ten-year review of Songdo IBD in South Korea examines the new city district's performance in terms of sustainability, connectivity and quality of life.
items.article23Body:
Songdo IBD is a new city district built on reclaimed land near Incheon. The masterplan integrates business, residential and cultural uses with a focus on sustainability and smart infrastructure. A ten-year review examines the district's performance in terms of sustainability, connectivity and quality of life.

The review will inform future masterplanning work in Asia and beyond.
items.article24Title: Carré d'Art in Nîmes: thirty years of culture and light
items.article24Summary: The Carré d'Art in Nîmes, facing the Roman Maison Carrée, marks thirty years as a museum of contemporary art and municipal library.
items.article24Body:
The Carré d'Art in Nîmes faces the Roman Maison Carrée and houses a museum of contemporary art and a municipal library. The transparent ground floor and classical proportions engage with the historic square. The building marks thirty years of operation and has become a symbol of the city's commitment to culture and heritage.

A programme of events will celebrate the anniversary throughout the year.
items.article25Title: Young Architects Programme 2026 opens for applications
items.article25Summary: The Young Architects Programme offers emerging practices the chance to design a temporary pavilion; applications for the 2026 edition are now open.
items.article25Body:
The Young Architects Programme gives emerging practices the opportunity to design and build a temporary pavilion that will be installed for one season. The programme supports innovation and experimentation and has launched the careers of many architects. Applications for the 2026 edition are now open.

Shortlisted teams will receive a stipend and technical support to develop and realise their proposals.
items.article26Title: Biophilic design and wellbeing: new research findings
items.article26Summary: New research from the practice examines the relationship between biophilic design, indoor environmental quality and occupant wellbeing in offices.
items.article26Body:
The practice has published new research on the relationship between biophilic design, indoor environmental quality and occupant wellbeing in offices. The study draws on post-occupancy data from several projects and compares environments with varying levels of natural light, greenery and connection to the outdoors.

Findings suggest that well-designed biophilic elements can support wellbeing and productivity. The full report is available on request.
items.article27Title: AIA Honor Award for Bloomberg European Headquarters
items.article27Summary: The Bloomberg European Headquarters has received an AIA Honor Award for architecture, recognising its contribution to sustainable commercial design and the public realm.
items.article27Body: The American Institute of Architects has awarded an Honor Award for architecture to the Bloomberg European Headquarters in London. The award recognises the building's contribution to sustainable commercial design, its integration with the historic street pattern and its generous public spaces. The project was completed in 2017 and has since become a reference for high-performance, architecturally ambitious offices.
items.article28Summary: A new design guide sets out how to achieve carbon-neutral office buildings through passive design, renewables and embodied carbon reduction.
items.article28Body:
The practice has released a design guide for carbon-neutral offices. The guide sets out how to achieve net-zero operational and embodied carbon through passive design, renewable energy, material selection and circular economy principles. It draws on experience from recent projects and aligns with leading sustainability frameworks.

The guide is intended for clients, developers and design teams and is available as a downloadable document.
items.article29Title: Parametric facades: from design to fabrication
items.article29Summary: A technical paper describes how parametric design and digital fabrication are being used to produce complex facades with improved performance and reduced waste.
items.article29Body:
A new technical paper describes how parametric design and digital fabrication are being used to produce complex facades with improved environmental performance and reduced material waste. The paper covers design workflows, structural and environmental analysis, and the link to manufacturing and site assembly.

Case studies include recent projects in Europe and Asia. The paper has been presented at an international conference and will be published in a peer-reviewed journal.
items.article30Summary: The practice's annual workplace wellbeing report examines how office design has evolved post-pandemic and what employees and employers expect from the workplace.
items.article30Body:
The practice's annual workplace wellbeing report has been published. The report examines how office design has evolved since the pandemic and what employees and employers now expect from the workplace. Topics include flexibility, collaboration spaces, indoor air quality and the role of the office in supporting mental health and productivity.

The report is based on surveys, post-occupancy evaluations and interviews with clients and is available to download from the practice website.
